_meta.note: System lifecycle N-D-C for the maintained C3 photosynthetic apparatus. Four lifecycle phases analogous to the gold system lifecycle: Resource (leaf/chloroplast design), Develop (chloroplast biogenesis), Operate (active photosynthesis), Sustain (repair and protection).

0.name: Resource Definition
0.description: Leaf morphology, chloroplast ultrastructure, pigment system design. The genetic and developmental blueprint that determines the photosynthetic capacity before the system becomes operational.
0.D_parameters: Genome-encoded protein stoichiometries; thylakoid stacking (grana:stroma ratio); leaf thickness and mesophyll conductance; chloroplast number per cell; light-harvesting complex gene expression
0.C_parameters: Photosynthetic capacity per unit leaf area; antenna size plasticity (shade/sun acclimation); chloroplast positioning (avoidance movement); stomatal density and aperture range
0.measurable_output: Maximum photosynthetic capacity (Amax); chlorophyll content; Fv/Fm
0.output_unit: µmol CO2 m-2 s-1; mg Chl m-2; dimensionless
0.notes: The photosynthetic resource definition is embedded in the leaf developmental program. Plasticity is significant: shade-adapted leaves have larger antenna (lower D constraint from limited light) but less Rubisco (lower C). The resource definition phase is well-understood genetically but in vivo proteome stoichiometry in specific conditions is partially opaque.

1.name: Develop and Commission
1.description: Chloroplast biogenesis during leaf expansion; photosystem assembly; chlorophyll biosynthesis; thylakoid membrane formation. The commissioning of a fully functional photosynthetic apparatus.
1.D_parameters: Chloroplast import machinery (TOC/TIC translocon); plastid gene expression for core subunits (PsbA D1, PsaA); assembly chaperones (Ycf3 for PSI; HCF136 for PSII); chlorophyll biosynthesis enzyme availability; regulatory coordination between nuclear and plastid genomes
1.C_parameters: Functional PSII and PSI reaction centers assembled; thylakoid membrane stacking established; Calvin cycle enzyme complement synthesized; full photosynthetic capacity reached by leaf expansion completion
1.measurable_output: Chlorophyll content during leaf ontogeny; functional PSII reaction center count; maximum quantum yield Fv/Fm achieved
1.output_unit: mg Chl m-2; PSII centers m-2; dimensionless
1.notes: Chloroplast development from proplastid to mature chloroplast is well-characterized. Full photosynthetic capacity is reached by leaf expansion completion in most C3 species. The assembly machinery (TOC/TIC, assembly chaperones) is well-documented. High balance score reflects the tight coordination between nuclear and plastid genome expression.

2.name: Operate
2.description: Active photosynthesis during the photoperiod across the plant's growing season. The fully operational phase converting light energy to chemical energy and carbon compounds.
2.D_parameters: Light availability and distribution within canopy; CO2 supply through stomata; temperature constraints on enzyme kinetics; water availability for stomatal conductance; nutrient (N Fe Mg) supply for enzyme maintenance
2.C_parameters: Net CO2 assimilation An; O2 evolution; sucrose and starch production; contribution to plant growth; contribution to ecosystem carbon balance; oxygen release to atmosphere
2.measurable_output: Net CO2 assimilation rate; daily carbon gain per unit leaf area; seasonal GPP
2.output_unit: µmol CO2 m-2 s-1; g C m-2 day-1; g C m-2 season-1
2.notes: The operational phase is the most well-measured in all of plant biology. Gas exchange, chlorophyll fluorescence, and remote sensing provide data from leaf to ecosystem scale. The C slightly exceeds D because the system self-regulates and integrates with downstream sinks effectively under non-stress conditions.

3.name: Sustain and Assure
3.description: Continuous repair and protection systems that maintain photosynthetic function against damage. Includes D1 protein turnover in PSII, carotenoid photoprotection, antioxidant systems, and seasonal acclimation.
3.D_parameters: D1 protein synthesis rate (must match photodamage rate); carotenoid biosynthesis for photoprotection; ascorbate peroxidase and superoxide dismutase activity; Rubisco activase demand under heat; FtsH protease complex for D1 degradation; RNA helicase for plastid mRNA folding
3.C_parameters: Maintained quantum yield under prolonged illumination; recovery from photoinhibition overnight; thermal tolerance through heat shock proteins; seasonal acclimation (nitrogen reallocation from Rubisco to antenna under shade; reverse under high light)
3.measurable_output: Recovery of Fv/Fm after high-light stress; D1 protein turnover rate; carotenoid content; antioxidant enzyme activity
3.output_unit: dimensionless (Fv/Fm); D1 molecules PSII-1 h-1; µmol carotenoids m-2; enzyme activity units
3.notes: The sustaining layer is the D-C imbalanced phase at lifecycle level. D (repair demands) exceeds C (repair capacity) under sustained high light or chronic stress, resulting in progressive photoinhibition. D1 protein turnover is well-characterized but the in vivo proteostasis network maintaining all photosystem subunits is only partially mapped. This is the lifecycle bottleneck.

lifecycle_system.interpretation: The C3 photosynthesis system lifecycle is highly coherent in its development and operational phases. The key lifecycle bottleneck is the Sustain and Assure phase (Phase 3), where repair demand (D) exceeds repair capacity (C) under sustained stress. This is the biological analog of infrastructure maintenance debt: the photosystem accumulates damage faster than it can be repaired under chronic high-light or heat conditions, leading to progressive performance decline.
